claims.text: Conventionally powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components typically exhibit residual stresses.
Conventionally powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components typically exhibit microsegregation.
Conventionally powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components typically exhibit porosity.
Conventionally powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components typically exhibit dimensional distortion.
An in-situ laser annealing pass after each consolidated layer will lower residual stress.
An in-situ laser annealing pass after each consolidated layer will reduce microstructural heterogeneity.
In-situ laser annealing will reduce microsegregation.
In-situ laser annealing will reduce porosity.
In-situ laser annealing will refine the grain structure.
Controlled thermal exposure from in-situ laser annealing promotes localized diffusion and microstructural reorganization.
The added thermal treatment alleviates residual stresses accumulated during layer-by-layer buildup.
The added thermal treatment heals defects and thereby reduces porosity.
Reduced residual stress, lower porosity, and grain refinement collectively improve dimensional control and mechanical properties.
Relative to standard powder-bed fusion, in-situ laser annealing will reduce warping and dimensional deviation.
Relative to standard powder-bed fusion, in-situ laser annealing will increase yield strength.
Relative to standard powder-bed fusion, in-situ laser annealing will increase ductility.
The intervention will be most effective in components with large thermal gradients and cooling conditions that otherwise produce pronounced defects.
The intervention's effectiveness will vary with alloy composition, geometric complexity, and layer thickness.
Prior studies of thermal treatments in additive manufacturing suggest benefits for stress relief.
Prior studies of thermal treatments in additive manufacturing suggest benefits for microstructural refinement.
